exposure: Cervical length measured by transvaginal ultrasonography (TVUS) at 20-24 weeks of gestation
cohort: 105 pregnant women with singleton pregnancies enrolled at 20-24 weeks gestation.
finding: Shorter ultrasonographic cervical length at 20-24 weeks gestation is significantly associated with an increased risk of spontaneous preterm birth and earlier gestational age at delivery.
gest_age: Mothers were 20-24 weeks gestation at enrollment; babies were born at various gestational ages, ranging from preterm (<37 weeks) to term (>=37 weeks).
